description: Shared TS<->PY test vector pinning the app-id resolution priority order (audit-app-framework-2026-07-02 D4; AL-1.4a). Consumed by packages/plugin/tests/appIdResolution.test.mjs (apps/appIdentity.appIdOf, re-exported as appScriptRegistry.appIdOf) and packages/admin/tests/test_app_id_resolution_fixture.py (applications/app_identity.resolve_app_id, re-exported as app_integrity_coverage.resolve_app_id). AL-1.4a put the canonical `app_id` at the head of the order — app_id > pkg_id > id > spec_id > instance_id — and collapsed the two implementations into ONE resolver per language, so the order can now only change in one place per side and this vector is what holds those two places together. expected_id: null means 'no id resolves' — each side maps null to its own documented fallback (TS 'unknown', PY ''). THE TRIM DIVERGENCE IS GONE: TS used to return the raw value where PY stripped it, so a manifest whose id carried stray whitespace produced two different coverage keys and the badge could never clear for it; both sides now strip, and the *_is_trimmed cases below pin that. Case is still NOT normalized at resolve time — the resolver never rewrites an id. What changed is narrower: it either honors a conforming `app_id` VERBATIM or declines it and falls through to the legacy chain, so an uppercase value (which APP_ID_PATTERN rejects) is no longer returned as canonical — uppercase_app_id_is_not_honored pins that, replacing the former app_id_case_is_preserved case. Normalization still belongs to the stamp (app_identity.canonical_app_id), which refuses to rewrite an id rather than silently re-identify an app. THE `app_id` NAME WAS NOT FREE: gallery/index.json has carried an `app_id` key since #3413 holding the app SCRIPT name (app_task_manager, which fails APP_ID_PATTERN), so the field is honored only when its value is a conforming slug. The legacy cases stay green through 1.4a/1.4b and are dropped in 1.4c when the fallback goes.
